page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with a massive 219.0 GB of system memory, yielding 54.69 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 262 GB local SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPUs are included, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the M8-4ms prioritizes memory capacity over raw processing speed. Its CPU performance is modest, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1035.08 and a multi-core score of 2724.76. Passmark CPU tests align with these findings, showing a CPU score of 3277.47 and a physics test score of 426.26. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with read-only large block bandwidth at 17.71 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 17.19 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 2.63 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 3.0 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the M8-4ms is its high memory-to-CPU ratio, which provides exceptional resource density for memory-bound tasks but offers limited compute power. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads that require large memory footprints without demanding high CPU performance. It is highly suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. However, it is poorly suited for compute-heavy tasks, software compilation, or LLM inference, as demonstrated by its low Geekbench compiling score of 2650.0 and prompt processing speed of 142.04 tokens per second on a small 135M model.
